name: Geiranger Village Center
tagline: The fjord-head hub where everything happens
description: The compact waterfront heart of the village, where the ferry quay, hotels, shops, cafes and the fjord center cluster within an easy walk. It is the most convenient base for services, dining and boat trips, and the busiest spot when cruise ships are in port.
vibe: Scenic, walkable, tourist-focused and lively in season
bestFor: First-time visitors who want services, ferries and dining on foot
pros: Direct access to the sightseeing ferry and tours
Best choice of hotels, cafes and shops
cons: Crowded and busy on cruise days
Highest prices and scarce long-stay housing

name: Flydalsjuvet / Dalsnibba Heights
tagline: Above the village on the mountain viewpoint road
description: The high ground on the Dalsnibba road south of the village, home to the famous Flydalsjuvet overlook and, higher still, the Dalsnibba skywalk. Scattered lodges and cabins here trade walkable convenience for elevation, quiet and some of the most iconic panoramas over the fjord.
bestFor: Photographers and drivers chasing the classic viewpoints
pros: Easy launch point for mountain drives
cons: Far from restaurants and services on foot

name: Hellesylt
tagline: The fjord's other gateway across the water
description: The small village at the western end of the Geiranger-Hellesylt ferry, set beside its own waterfall and the mouth of the Sunnylvsfjord. Quieter and cheaper than Geiranger, it makes a calm base for those happy to ride the scenic ferry in for the marquee sights.
vibe: Low-key, workaday and calmer than Geiranger
bestFor: Slow travelers wanting a quieter, cheaper fjord base
pros: Direct scenic ferry link to Geiranger
Its own waterfall and relaxed feel
cons: Depends on ferry timings to reach Geiranger

name: Stranda
tagline: A proper small town within reach of the fjord
description: A larger town northwest of Geiranger, on the Storfjord and known for its ski area and its cured meats. Stranda offers more shops, services and year-round life than the fjord villages, making it a practical, better-stocked base for longer stays and winter trips.
bestFor: Longer stays needing real services and winter access
pros: More shops, groceries and year-round amenities
cons: Not on the fjord's headline scenery
A drive and ferry from Geiranger itself
